newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin not going to NATO summit - Interfax.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin not going to NATO summit - Interfax.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin has no plans to attend next July's NATO summit which is due to offer membership to some former Soviet bloc states, Interfax news agency quoted his spokesman as saying on Saturday.

"I will venture to say that participation at the forthcoming Madrid meeting...has never been seriously considered by the top Russian leadership," said Sergei Yastrzhembsky, noting that the Madrid summit did not appear on Yeltsin's working schedule.

Yastrzhembsky, who was speaking to Interfax in the Black Sea resort of Sochi where Yeltsin is on holiday, said the Russian position on attending did not depend on getting an invitation from the western defence pact.
He added that Russian officials had plenty of opportunity to exchange opinions with NATO and its leading members.

Russian officials led by Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov are urgently negotiating a deal with NATO which Yeltsin has said he hopes to sign in Paris on May 27. The Kremlin, which is vehemently opposed to NATO's expansion, wants a say in the enlarged bloc and formal guarantees on its security.

Some western officials, notably in Washington, doubt that differences between the two sides can be overcome by May 27. Some western leaders appeared to believe Yeltsin would attend the Madrid meeting if a deal was reached, but the Kremlin had previously said it was not sure that the president would go.
